nodes.summary: Vaal Architect of Atziri who, per a carving in the Howling Caves, secretly built a vault in a remote mountain, hiding the 'treason' from the Queen and sending his children into it; his name is on a Temple Console medallion. Thought the Queen mad.

nodes.name: Ursea, The Matron
nodes.summary: Named in Act 5 datamine as a boss/text-audio entry. Unreleased; no lore available.

nodes.name: Vandroth, Blackblooded Enslaver
nodes.summary: Abyssal boss said by guides to drop Kulemak's Invitation (shared with Tasgul).
sources: Abyssal Commanders Tasgul and Vandroth drop Kulemak Invitation

nodes.name: Vel Anxa
nodes.summary: Priest 'of the Order' listed as a Twilight Order member under Torvian, Hand of the Saviour. No further detail in sources read.

nodes.name: Viper Napuatzi
nodes.summary: Vaal general of Utzaal's past who captures Alva and sends her to Doryani; defeated in the Utzaal time-gate sequence.

alt_summaries.summary: General of the Vaal legion in the Timeless Conflict. (General of the Vaal legion in Legion league, 3.7.0.)

Vaal warrior in Utzaal's past who confronts the Exile and Alva after the gate opens, accuses them of spilling Vaal blood, and has Alva taken to Doryani; defeated by the Exile in Act 3 (exact rank/title not given in the wiki quest log).

nodes.name: Vorana
nodes.summary: Black Scythe mercenary leader and Medved's beloved. She killed the twelve priests who stabbed Olroth, took gem-infused rites into her own flesh and left the walls. Returns as the boss Vorana, Last to Fall.

chronology.relative: Expedition era, thousands of years before PoE1

sources: section 'The Kalguur' (Broken Circle, Priesthood, Medved's challenge)
Medved, Vorana and Uhtred join Olroth as the 4 Faction Leaders

alt_summaries.summary: Black Scythes mercenary leader who took up gems and fought on; later Vorana, Last to Fall.
Leader of the Black Scythe mercenaries; used virtue gems against the nightbreeds and the Empty-Eyed Fiend, casting aside her primary virtue.
Expedition faction leader, 'Vorana, Last to Fall', fought in a tomb on the islands in The Grand Expedition.

nodes.name: Vornas, the Fell Flame
nodes.summary: Vornas, the Fell Flame is a boss the Exile defeats after passing the Galai Gates during the Recruit the Maraketh interlude.
sources: Quest log, 'Defeat Vornas, the Fell Flame.'

nodes.name: Vruun, Marshal of Xesht
nodes.summary: PoE2 boss in Unstable Breaches, marshal serving Xesht; drops Lineage supports.
sources: Version History: introduced in 0.5.0; boss in Unstable Breaches

alt_summaries.summary: Breach marshal found in stabilised Unstable Breaches; Ailith's PoE1 Keepers quest asks the Exile to bring 'The Head of Vruun' and praises it as preparation for a second graft meld.
Breach boss in Unstable Breach encounters; drops the Head of Vruun used to grow the Grasping Orchid; introduced 0.5.0.

nodes.name: Xibaqua
nodes.summary: Mythic/historical figure of the Vaal Empire whose remains were believed to be the progenitor of all Vaal; Vaal myth says their conflict with 'the gods' produced a 'droplet of pure light', the first Vaal. Unclear whether myth or history.

alt_summaries.summary: Historical figure of the Vaal Empire whose remains were believed to be the original progenitor of all Vaal; born from flesh of ancient Vaal gods; named on a Glorious Vanity variant.

nodes.name: Xipocado, Royal Architect
nodes.summary: Atziri's Royal Architect who with Doryani rebuilt the temple as a self-modifying machine; boss in the Temple of Atzoatl (PoE1) and Atziri's Temple (PoE2).

alt_summaries.summary: Boss of Atziri's Temple; in PoE1 an enemy in past Temple of Atzoatl who built the Royal Meeting Room to Atziri's throne.

nodes.name: Xyclucian, the Chimera
nodes.summary: Unique chimera guarding the entrance to Jiquani's Machinarium; drops the Chimeral Inscribed Ultimatum.

alt_summaries.summary: Unique chimera guarding the way to Jiquani's Machinarium in the Chimeral Wetlands (PoE2 Act 3).

nodes.name: Yama the White
nodes.summary: Boss of the Halls of the Dead, fought as Yama's Test: 'Old Yama see if worthy of Hinekora!'

nodes.name: Zalmarath, the Colossus
nodes.summary: Colossus guarding the Titan Grotto; holds the Flame Ruby for the Rite of Flame.

nodes.name: Zarka
nodes.summary: Ardura Maraketh elder who runs the caravan, recreates the Horn of the Vastiri with the Exile, and gives the Exile the status of jingakh.
sources: Quest log 'Recreate the Horn of the Vastiri'

nodes.name: Zarokh, Grand Djinn of Time
nodes.summary: Djinn who siphons other djinn to project power; his mirage is bound by an Astral Chain.
sources: Zarokh, the Temporal: complete all four Sekhemas floors

alt_summaries.summary: Final boss of the Trial of the Sekhemas (after all four floors) according to a guide.

nodes.name: Zicoatl, Warden of the Core
nodes.summary: Construct guardian of the Large Soul Core in Jiquani's Sanctum.
sources: Quest 'Defeat Zicoatl, Warden of the Core'

alt_summaries.summary: Warden guarding the large Soul Core in Jiquani's Sanctum.

nodes.name: Zolin and Zelina
nodes.summary: Cuachic Blood Priest (Zolin) and Blood Priestess (Zelina), apparently siblings and High Priests of the Cuachic Vault who kept the Cuachic numbed and controlled; defeated by the Exile in Interlude 3 and persuaded by Doryani's code phrase 'the time of the sparrow has come'.
sources: Defeat Zolin and Zelina; Speak to Doryani
'The Cuachic Legacy' / 'The Cuachic Purpose' (writer refers to 'my sister')

alt_summaries.summary: Cuachic Vaal blood priest and priestess guarding the Cuachic Vault; recognise Doryani and pledge to march to war.

nodes.name: The Abyss
nodes.summary: Cracks and pits that spawn monsters when approached; source of abyss jewels, Stygian Vises and the Abyssal Depths in PoE1 Abyss league (3.1.0); PoE2 Rise of the Abyssal (0.3.0) revives Abysses with the Well of Souls and desecration.

nodes.name: Abyssal Depths (PoE2)
nodes.summary: Underground realm accessed from some Abyss fissures; in 0.5 three Abyssal faction bosses guard it and yield the key to the Well of Souls (community guide).
sources: League content: access to the Abyssal Depths

nodes.name: Ancient Beacons
nodes.summary: Vaal devices that fuel Atziri's Temple when monsters are sacrificed to them; six open a portal to the Vaal Ruins.

nodes.name: Ascendancy
nodes.summary: Ascendancy classes unlock through trials. In PoE1 the Lord's Labyrinth quest leads to the Trials of Ascendancy; in PoE2 the Ascension Trials (Sekhemas, Chaos) grant ascendancy points.
sources: infobox: objective 'Finish the Trials of Ascendancy to access ... Labyrinth'

alt_summaries.summary: Power granted to the exile who completes Izaro's Lord's Labyrinth trials; framed as inheriting the Labyrinth's succession test.

nodes.name: Abyssal Lich (PoE2 Ascendancy)
nodes.summary: Alternate Witch ascendancy that absorbs the powers of the Well of Souls; unlocked by defeating the Vessel of Kulemak at full power after ascending to Lich.
sources: section 'Overview': 'The Abyssal Lich is a Lich that has absorbed the powers of the Well of Souls, gaining the undying power of the Abyssal, replacing some of its Ascendancy passives with alternates.'

section 'Alternate ascendancy classes': 'Currently, the Abyssal Lich is the only alternate ascendancy available and is unlocked by defeating Vessel of Kulemak at full power while the player has already ascended into a Lich.'
section 'witch' base-class mapping: 'Her Ascendancy classes are the Infernalist, Blood Mage, and Lich.'

nodes.name: Acolyte of Chayula (PoE2 Ascendancy)
nodes.summary: Monk ascendancy that has uncovered the secrets of the Dreamer (Chayula) and embraces chaos damage: Embrace the Darkness, Waking Dream and Flames of Chayula.
sources: section 'Overview': 'The Acolyte of Chayula has uncovered the secrets of the Dreamer and embraced the madness which entail it.'
section 'Overview': 'Ascendancies can be unlocked by completing Ascension Trials through the campaign and endgame.'
section 'monk' base-class mapping: 'His ascendancy classes are the Invoker, Acolyte of Chayula, and Martial Artist.'

nodes.name: Amazon (PoE2 Ascendancy)
nodes.summary: Huntress ascendancy: an elite warrior trained to protect the Azmeri elders (Elemental Infusion, Predatory Instinct, Azmeri Brew).
sources: section 'Overview': 'The Amazon is an elite warrior trained to protect the Azmeri elders, transforming her into an offensive powerhouse with recovery and Evasion bonuses to boot.'
section 'Overview': 'Ascendancies can be unlocked by completing Ascension Trials through the campaign and endgame.'
section 'huntress' base-class mapping: 'Her ascendancy classes are the Ritualist, Amazon, and Spirit Walker.'

nodes.name: Blood Mage (PoE2 Ascendancy)
nodes.summary: Witch ascendancy trading Life for power (Sanguimancy, Life Remnants).
sources: section 'Overview': 'The Blood Mage puts her Life on the line in exchange for power.'
section 'Overview': 'Ascendancies can be unlocked by completing Ascension Trials through the campaign and endgame.'
section 'witch' base-class mapping: 'Her Ascendancy classes are the Infernalist, Blood Mage, and Lich.'

nodes.name: Chronomancer (PoE2 Ascendancy)
nodes.summary: Sorceress ascendancy manipulating time (Time Snap, Time Freeze, Temporal Rift).
sources: section 'Overview': 'The Chronomancer can manipulate time, gaining access to a variety of utility skills and other bonuses.'
section 'Overview': 'Ascendancies can be unlocked by completing Ascension Trials through the campaign and endgame.'
section 'sorceress' base-class mapping: 'Her ascendancy classes are the Stormweaver, Chronomancer, and Disciple of Varashta.'

nodes.name: Deadeye (PoE2 Ascendancy)
nodes.summary: Ranger ascendancy focused on ranged offence (projectile damage, Tailwind, Called Shots).
sources: section 'Overview': 'The Deadeye is a class focused around ranged offense.'
section 'Overview': 'Ascendancies can be unlocked by completing Ascension Trials through the campaign and endgame.'
section 'ranger' base-class mapping: 'Her ascendancy classes are the Deadeye and Pathfinder.'

nodes.name: Disciple of Varashta (PoE2 Ascendancy)
nodes.summary: Sorceress ascendancy that commands three Djinns (Ruzhan, Navira, Kelari) bound to serve Sekhema Varashta as penance.
sources: section 'Overview': 'The Disciple of Varashta can employ the services of Djinns who are bound to serve the great Sekhema Varashta as penance.'
section 'Overview': 'Ascendancies can be unlocked by completing Ascension Trials through the campaign and endgame.'
section 'sorceress' base-class mapping: 'Her ascendancy classes are the Stormweaver, Chronomancer, and Disciple of Varashta.'

nodes.name: Gemling Legionnaire (PoE2 Ascendancy)
nodes.summary: Mercenary ascendancy embedded with the potential of virtue gems; passives scale with the gems socketed.
sources: section 'Overview': 'The Gemling Legionnaire is embedded with the true potential of virtue gems, unlocking new powers.'
section 'Overview': 'Ascendancies can be unlocked by completing Ascension Trials through the campaign and endgame.'
section 'mercenary' base-class mapping: 'His ascendancy classes are the Witchhunter, Gemling Legionnaire, and Tactician.'

nodes.name: Infernalist (PoE2 Ascendancy)
nodes.summary: Witch ascendancy calling on demonic forces (Pyromantic Pact, Infernal Flame) and three contracts with Beidat.
sources: section 'Overview': 'The Infernalist calls upon demonic forces to unleash hellish flames and gain great power at a cost.'
section 'Overview': 'Ascendancies can be unlocked by completing Ascension Trials through the campaign and endgame.'
section 'witch' base-class mapping: 'Her Ascendancy classes are the Infernalist, Blood Mage, and Lich.'

nodes.name: Invoker (PoE2 Ascendancy)
nodes.summary: Monk ascendancy attuned to nature and the elements (Elemental Expression, Unbound Avatar).
sources: section 'Overview': 'The Invoker is attuned to nature, providing mastery over the elements.'
section 'Overview': 'Ascendancies can be unlocked by completing Ascension Trials through the campaign and endgame.'
section 'monk' base-class mapping: 'His ascendancy classes are the Invoker, Acolyte of Chayula, and Martial Artist.'

nodes.name: Lich (PoE2 Ascendancy)
nodes.summary: Witch ascendancy become one with death (everlasting curses, Unholy Might, Crystalline Phylactery, Soulless Form).
sources: section 'Overview': 'The Lich is a class who has become one with death, unlocking the potential to acquire great power at a price.'
section 'Overview': 'Ascendancies can be unlocked by completing Ascension Trials through the campaign and endgame.'
section 'witch' base-class mapping: 'Her Ascendancy classes are the Infernalist, Blood Mage, and Lich.'

nodes.name: Martial Artist (PoE2 Ascendancy)
nodes.summary: Monk ascendancy specialising in Hollow techniques (illusions, bells) and combos.
sources: section 'Overview': 'The Martial Artist has perfected his mind and body to master the art of Hollow techniques.'
section 'Overview': 'Ascendancies can be unlocked by completing Ascension Trials through the campaign and endgame.'
section 'monk' base-class mapping: 'His ascendancy classes are the Invoker, Acolyte of Chayula, and Martial Artist.'

nodes.name: Oracle (PoE2 Ascendancy)
nodes.summary: Druid ascendancy using Foresight (Fateful Vision, Converging Paths, Forced Outcome).
sources: section 'Overview': 'The Oracle uses the power of Foresight to outmatch his foes and unlock new abilities.'
section 'Overview': 'Ascendancies can be unlocked by completing Ascension Trials through the campaign and endgame.'
section 'druid' base-class mapping: 'His ascendancy classes are the Shaman and Oracle.'

nodes.name: Pathfinder (PoE2 Ascendancy)
nodes.summary: Ranger ascendancy specialising in flasks, mobility and survival (Enduring Elixirs).
sources: section 'Overview': 'The Pathfinder is a survival specialist with a focus in flasks, mobility, and flexibility with the passive skill tree.'
section 'Overview': 'Ascendancies can be unlocked by completing Ascension Trials through the campaign and endgame.'
section 'ranger' base-class mapping: 'Her ascendancy classes are the Deadeye and Pathfinder.'

nodes.name: Ritualist (PoE2 Ascendancy)
nodes.summary: Huntress ascendancy using the darker Azmeri arts (Corrupted Lifeforce, Blood Boils, Ritual Sacrifice).
sources: section 'Overview': 'The Ritualist has adopted the darker arts of the Azmeri.'
section 'Overview': 'Ascendancies can be unlocked by completing Ascension Trials through the campaign and endgame.'
section 'huntress' base-class mapping: 'Her ascendancy classes are the Ritualist, Amazon, and Spirit Walker.'

nodes.name: Shaman (PoE2 Ascendancy)
nodes.summary: Druid ascendancy unleashing the force of nature (Druidic Champion, Furious Wellspring, Turning of the Season).
sources: section 'Overview': 'The Shaman unleashes the force of nature upon his foes.'
section 'Overview': 'Ascendancies can be unlocked by completing Ascension Trials through the campaign and endgame.'
section 'druid' base-class mapping: 'His ascendancy classes are the Shaman and Oracle.'

nodes.name: Smith of Kitava (PoE2 Ascendancy)
nodes.summary: Warrior ascendancy whose blacksmithing draws on the power of Kitava (Manifest Weapon, Temper Weapon, Heat of the Forge).
sources: section 'Overview': 'The Smith of Kitava has honed his blacksmithing with the power of the god Kitava.'
section 'Overview': 'Ascendancies can be unlocked by completing Ascension Trials through the campaign and endgame.'
section 'warrior' base-class mapping: 'His ascendancy classes are the Titan, Warbringer, and Smith of Kitava.'

nodes.name: Spirit Walker (PoE2 Ascendancy)
nodes.summary: Huntress ascendancy blessed by Azmeri spirits in three animal forms (Vivid Stampede, Primal Bounty, Wild Protector).
sources: section 'Overview': 'The Spirit Walker has received the blessings of the Azmeri spirits, taking the form of three different animal spirits.'
section 'Overview': 'Ascendancies can be unlocked by completing Ascension Trials through the campaign and endgame.'
section 'huntress' base-class mapping: 'Her ascendancy classes are the Ritualist, Amazon, and Spirit Walker.'

nodes.name: Stormweaver (PoE2 Ascendancy)
nodes.summary: Sorceress ascendancy, an arcane master of the elements (chill or shock, Elemental Storms, Arcane Surge).
sources: section 'Overview': 'The Stormweaver is an arcane master of the elements.'
section 'Overview': 'Ascendancies can be unlocked by completing Ascension Trials through the campaign and endgame.'
section 'sorceress' base-class mapping: 'Her ascendancy classes are the Stormweaver, Chronomancer, and Disciple of Varashta.'

nodes.name: Tactician (PoE2 Ascendancy)
nodes.summary: Mercenary ascendancy specialising in defences and empowering allies (Banners, Pin, Supporting Fire).
sources: section 'Overview': 'The Tactician is a class specializing in defenses and empowering allies.'
section 'Overview': 'Ascendancies can be unlocked by completing Ascension Trials through the campaign and endgame.'
section 'mercenary' base-class mapping: 'His ascendancy classes are the Witchhunter, Gemling Legionnaire, and Tactician.'

nodes.name: Titan (PoE2 Ascendancy)
nodes.summary: Warrior ascendancy of vitality and might: ancestrally boosted slams, Heavy Stuns, more life and armour.
sources: section 'Overview': 'The Titan is a class that possesses tremendous vitality and might.'
section 'Overview': 'Ascendancies can be unlocked by completing Ascension Trials through the campaign and endgame.'
section 'warrior' base-class mapping: 'His ascendancy classes are the Titan, Warbringer, and Smith of Kitava.'

nodes.name: Warbringer (PoE2 Ascendancy)
nodes.summary: Warrior ascendancy drawing strength from Karui and Ezomyte ancestry (totems and Ancestral Spirits, jade, Break Armour).
sources: section 'Overview': 'The Warbringer draws strength from his Karui and Ezomyte ancestry.'
section 'Overview': 'Ascendancies can be unlocked by completing Ascension Trials through the campaign and endgame.'
section 'warrior' base-class mapping: 'His ascendancy classes are the Titan, Warbringer, and Smith of Kitava.'

nodes.name: Witchhunter (PoE2 Ascendancy)
nodes.summary: Mercenary ascendancy and boss killer (Culling Strike, Decimating Strike, Sorcery Ward).
sources: section 'Overview': 'The Witchhunter has access to passives that grant general offensive bonuses, as well as specialized bonuses towards certain types of enemies.'
section 'Overview': 'Ascendancies can be unlocked by completing Ascension Trials through the campaign and endgame.'
section 'mercenary' base-class mapping: 'His ascendancy classes are the Witchhunter, Gemling Legionnaire, and Tactician.'

nodes.name: Ascension Trials
nodes.summary: PoE2's three-trial system (Sekhemas, Chaos, and a planned third) that gates ascendancy. Each trial is tied to a Wraeclastian culture. Four tiers of trials give 2 ascendancy points each for 8 total.

nodes.name: The Atlas of Worlds (concept)
nodes.summary: The endgame structure of PoE1: a web of alternate worlds ('maps') reached through the Map Device. Wiki lore says it was either found or created by the Elder as a hunting ground; after the Elder's defeat other powers (Maven, Eldritch Horrors, the Originator) contest it. PoE2 has its own, separate Atlas whose Precursor Towers are mentioned in PoE1 wiki lore.
sources: section 'The Atlas of Worlds' / 'The Elder and the Shaper'
lead: 'The Atlas of Worlds may have originally been created as a feeding ground for the Elder'

nodes.name: Azmeri Spirits and Wisps
nodes.summary: Azmeri spirits appear as wisps leading hunters to monsters, introduced with Dawn of the Hunt; Delwyn at Hunting Grounds teaches the hunt; the Spirit Walker ascendancy (0.5) controls Stag, Owl, Bear spirits.
sources: Spirit Walker (Huntress) master of Azmeri spirits

nodes.name: Gods as belief and Beast-energy
nodes.summary: Interpretive concept: gods in Wraeclast are sustained by worship and by proximity to the Beast's power; their abilities are 'restricted by the Beast'. Fan synthesis built from wiki statements on godhood and the Beast.
sources: Lore: 'Like the other gods of Wraeclast, Kitava's abilities are restricted by the Beast'
Halani found powerless from lack of worship (see PoE1 'God' page, Maraketh gods)

nodes.name: The Breach
nodes.summary: Otherworldly realm/phenomenon whose tears let Breach monsters enter Wraeclast; original Breach league (2.5.0) had breaches expanding as monsters are killed, splinters forming Breachstones for the five Breachlords' Domains. Replaced in 3.28.0 by the Keepers-of-the-Flame rework (Hiveborn, Ailith, Genesis Tree). PoE2 has Unstable Breaches and the Breachlords' lore (Xesht).
sources: version history 3.28.0: new Breach replaces original Breach mechanic

nodes.name: Breach and the Keepers of the Flame (PoE2 0.5)
nodes.summary: 0.5 Breach storyline: Ailith and the Keepers of the Flame hold back the Hiveborn from the Monastery of the Keepers; the Genesis Tree is a crafting hub; endgame Breach Domains end in Sky Fortresses with the Breachlords Tul and Esh, then Xesht.
sources: Breach: Ailith and the Keepers of the Flame hold back the Hiveborn

nodes.name: Cataclysm
nodes.summary: Lore term for the world-ending catastrophes that destroyed civilisations: the unknown cataclysm that wiped out the Precursors, the Vaal Cataclysm (also 'The Fall', c. 400 BIC), and the Eternal Empire Cataclysm (~1339 IC). The corpus uses the word for each event but does not define a single in-world category; this node groups those uses. Not the PoE2 epilogue quest 'Cataclysm's Wake', which is an Atlas tutorial quest.

chronology.relative: from the Precursor era to c. 1339 IC (several events)

sources: intro: 'An incredibly advanced precursor civilization existed, but was wiped out by an unknown cataclysm.'; section '====The Vaal Cataclysm====': 'The Vaal Cataclysm, also known as The Fall, was a historical event...'
section '===The Cataclysm (~1339 IC)===': 'The Cataclysm brought an end to Voll's reign and the Eternal Empire as a whole.'
page intro: 'Cataclysm's Wake is an epilogue quest. It act as the tutorial quest for the Atlas.'

nodes.name: Citadels (Iron, Copper, Stone)
nodes.summary: Three Atlas fortresses (Iron, Copper, Stone) whose bosses drop one Crisis Fragment each toward the Arbiter of Ash: Iron Citadel = Count Geonor, Copper Citadel = Jamanra, Stone Citadel = Doryani, Royal Thaumaturge (agreed by several guides; the poe2 wiki Doryani page also lists the Stone Citadel). The removed 0.1-0.4 epilogue quests Faridun Foray (boss listed Count Geonor), Ezomyte Infiltration (boss listed The Perennial King) and Vaal Incursion (boss Doryani) all start 'Investigate the Burning Monolith'; how The Perennial King maps to Jamanra is unclear. Fragment mapping differs between guides.
sources: quest infobox: boss Doryani, Royal Thaumaturge; start 'Investigate The Burning Monolith'; removed 0.5.0
quest infobox: boss Count Geonor; removed 0.5.0
quest infobox: boss The Perennial King; removed 0.5.0
can be found in endgame as a citadel boss in The Stone Citadel
Stone (Doryani), Copper (Jamanra), Iron (Count Geonor) - fragment mapping differs from other guides

nodes.name: Corruption
nodes.summary: Lore force of mutation and malformation tied to the Beast and its predecessors: the Beast 'possesses corrupting powers' that mutate whatever contacts it; Kitava is called 'God of Corruption' in Karui dialogue; Precursors mastered corruption and Doryani attempts to harness the Precursor Weapon to destroy corruption. Not the Corrupted-item mechanic.

chronology.relative: from the Precursor era onward (Beast, Vaal, Eternal Empire)

sources: intro: 'The Beast possesses corrupting powers, devouring the souls of his prey and mutating whoever comes in contact with it.'
section '==Kitava==' > Dialogue, Haku's 'Kaom' option: 'Kitava, God of Corruption, consumed Kaom from heart to skin.'
section '===Precursor civilization===': 'After mastering corruption, they delved deeper...'; the Precursor Weapon is one 'which Doryani attempts to harness to destroy corruption'

alt_summaries.summary: The in-world corrupting power named by the Karui and Vaal (Kitava as 'God of Corruption', worship of Corruption at a Vaal temple) and carried as the Seed of Corruption (what remains of the Beast) in PoE2. The item-corruption mechanic is a separate game system.

nodes.name: Crisis Fragments
nodes.summary: Fragments needed to open the sealed door of the Burning Monolith (Arbiter of Ash). In 0.1-0.4 three were needed (Ancient, Weathered, Faded), one per Citadel boss. In the 0.5 quest log only the Ancient and Weathered fragments are picked up in the Fortress Enigma Chambers; Citadels continue to drop them for repeat runs. Guides disagree on which Citadel drops which (most: Iron=Ancient, Copper=Faded, Stone=Weathered), and the quest log matches that for Geonor (Ancient) and Doryani (Weathered).
sources: Citadel-to-Arbiter loop; fragment mapping disagrees between guides

nodes.name: Delirium: The Hare and the Raven
nodes.summary: 0.5 Delirium storyline ('The Hare and the Raven' in the press release): Elder Madox is freed from a Delirium mirror (Strange Reflection), leads the Exile to the Withered Willow, and the Raven Trickster Tangmazu must be stopped. Official notes: 'An ancient Trickster God has been unleashed, spreading madness across Wraeclast.'
sources: Delirium (The Hare and the Raven): confrontation with Tangmazu
An ancient Trickster God has been unleashed

nodes.name: Doryani's contingencies
nodes.summary: Fan-synthesised reading of Doryani's secret preparations: anti-Beast Precursor weapon, flood-sealed Utzaal, and a time gateway needing Vaal blood. Interpretive; some details rest on tertiary YouTube analysis.

nodes.name: Exile (exile system)
nodes.summary: The exile system: criminals of Oriath are sentenced by the Templar government and shipped to Wraeclast. The sentence text reads 'You are hereby Exiled to Wraeclast where, it is hoped, you shall come to repent your Sins'. The player's character is one of these exiles. Precedent exists: under Tyndarus Phrecius, people were exiled to the land later called Trarthus. The wiki gives no single in-world reason for choosing Wraeclast.
sources: section 'The Present'; section 'Reign of Tyndarus Phrecius' (Trarthus exile)

nodes.name: Exile's Journey (Day Zero rule)
nodes.summary: The wiki's 'Day Zero' rule: each league's narrative starts with the Exile face-down in the sand of the Twilight Strand, having just been exiled by Dominus, so league stories cannot build on earlier leagues' events.
sources: section 'The Atlas of Worlds' (Day Zero rule)

nodes.name: Expedition and The Grand Expedition (PoE2)
nodes.summary: 0.5 Expedition storyline from Ruins of Kingsmarch: Rog searches for Gwennen across an ocean of islands, Medved, Vorana, Uhtred, Olroth lead factions; a Verisium meteor is the goal.
sources: Expedition: Rog searches for his missing wife, Gwennen

nodes.name: Ezomyte Runesmithing
nodes.summary: Rune craft with Kalguuran origins, revealed by Farrow in 0.5.
sources: Farrow reveals the Kalguuran origins of Ezomyte Runesmithing

nodes.name: Nature of godhood (ascension)
nodes.summary: In PoE lore a mortal of rare quality could ascend to godhood on the adoration of their people, shedding mortality; this became impossible once Sin created the Beast. Becoming a god often costs one's humanity. Gods can also be 'made' by belief of followers (Innocence's ascension was fuelled by hatred of Sin).

chronology.relative: before the creation of the Beast

sources: Sin, 'The Origins of the Gods': "There was a time before the Beast ... men and women like you could ascend. Through rareness of quality and the adoration of their people..."

nodes.name: Kalguuran runesmithing
nodes.summary: Kalguuran art of engraving starlight runes (Verisium from meteorites) into weapons and armour; Ezomytes learned it from the first expedition; revived as Runesmithing in Settlers and Runeforging in PoE2 Act 4.

nodes.name: Karui Gods
nodes.summary: The gods honoured within the Karui Way: Arohongui, Hinekora, Kitava, Ngamahu, Ramako, Tasalio, Tawhoa, Tukohama and Valako, as named on the Karui Gods page.
sources: intro: 'In the game's lore, The Karui Way has several gods that are representative of or rule over various aspects of the world.'

nodes.name: Karui Way (Makanui)
nodes.summary: Karui code of honour and traditions (Way of the Warrior); some who follow it forbid virtue gems for causing blood fever.

nodes.name: Leylines
nodes.summary: Ancient underground structures Doryani believes span the continent beneath the Ziggurat; they power the Waygate and resonate with the Precursor Tower.
sources: Doryani: This Ziggurat was built over what my ancestors called 'leylines'

nodes.name: Maraketh Shrine
nodes.summary: Room-reward shrines in the PoE2 Trial of the Sekhemas. Each shrine (Tabina, Balbala, Ahkeli or Galai variants) lets the player spend 5 Sacred Water to restore part of their Honour, with a random Boon or Minor Affliction on some variants; the Fountain of Youth minor boon restores 40 Honour when a Maraketh Shrine is venerated.
sources: Full page (stub): 'Maraketh Shrines are found as room rewards in the Trial of the Sekhemas'; shrine list (Honour Tabina / Balbala / Ahkeli / Galai); Fountain of Youth minor boon

nodes.name: Martyr of the First Edict (Void league leaderboard)
nodes.summary: Rise of the Abyssal mechanic: once per league a level-100 character can be sacrificed at the Site of the Chosen, sending it to the Void league and listing it as the 'Martyr of the First Edict' on the leaderboard. Meta/league flavour; no source explains the naming.
sources: paragraph: 'listed as the Martyr of the First Edict on the leaderboard'

nodes.name: Masters of the Atlas
nodes.summary: 0.5 storylines of three Atlas Masters: Jado (Order of the Djinn; unlocked by an anomaly map near the start), Hilda (monster hunter, Hilda's Campsite) and Doryani (unlocked by clearing a corruption nexus). The earlier draft's 'ascendancy-like specialisation' claim is unsupported and was removed.
sources: Atlas Masters: Jado, Hilda, Doryani; Doryani questline via corruption nexus; Jado via anomaly map

nodes.name: Atlas of Worlds (PoE2)
nodes.summary: The PoE2 endgame map network, reached after the campaign via Doryani's Waygate and navigated with Waystones. Rebuilt in 0.5 (Return of the Ancients) with fixed points of interest, storylines and a fully unlockable Atlas passive tree.
sources: quest log: 'Use the Map Device and the Waystone to enter a Map'
Atlas passive tree: Fully remade; zone quest chains

nodes.name: The Red Pyre
nodes.summary: Entity/title in Ailith's Word of the Dreamer ('The Red Pyre burns hot... The Dreamer once knew him, before his addiction'). The fire imagery and the book's subject (the four Breachlords that became Xesht) point to Xoph, Dark Embers; the identification is inferred, not stated.

nodes.name: Rite of the Nameless
nodes.summary: Ritual mechanic/quest stage: place the Head of the King on the Incomplete Effigy in Caer Tarth, use it to select five maps, complete Rituals there to collect effigy parts (Tangled Torso, Mossy Arm, Frayed Cloth, Brittle Arm, Ragged Cloth), activate the Effigy and perform the Rite to reach the Darkness and the Bodach. 0.5.5 campaign unique-boss Rituals work similarly.
sources: unique boss Rituals work similarly to the Rite of the Nameless

nodes.name: Ritual (altar mechanic)
nodes.summary: Ritual Altars spawn wave encounters inside a ritual circle; defeating monsters earns Favour/Tribute to buy items. PoE1 Ritual league gives no narrative; Vaal Ritual Altars may summon Atziri's Apparition; later Wildwood lore ties 'ritual altars' to the King in the Mists; PoE2 adopts it in Forbidden Rites.

nodes.name: Ritual and the King in the Mists (PoE2)
nodes.summary: 0.5 Ritual storyline: Aoife, a lost spirit bound by the King in the Mists, appeals to the Wildwood; the prison beneath holds the Bodach; the Rite of the Nameless in Caer Tarth. 0.5.5 adds Ritual altars to every zone.
sources: Ritual: Aoife, a lost spirit, bound by the King in the Mists... Bodach ... Rite of the Nameless

nodes.name: Rogue exiles
nodes.summary: Exiled criminals who roam Wraeclast as hostile NPCs; originated in Anarchy league (0.11.0), later reused in PoE2 (Lichborn exiles in Rise of the Abyssal).
sources: raising a rogue exile as Lichborn

nodes.name: Rogue Exiles (PoE2)
nodes.summary: Roaming exile NPC bosses introduced in 0.2.0; Abyss can raise a slain rogue exile as a Lichborn exile.
sources: raising a slain rogue exile as a Lichborn exile

nodes.name: Sekhema
nodes.summary: Maraketh leader title; always a woman chosen by merit and anointed with the feather of the Great Roc; tale-women keep the people's history.

nodes.name: The Edicts (Precursor murals)
nodes.summary: Series of vague Precursor murals described by the PoE2 wiki as depicting the Beast and possibly instructions on how to contain it; numbered First to Fourth in game. Known: Third = instrument is the Weapon (Hooded One recognises it as 'the Weapon I saw in that third mural'); Second = Doryani's guess that the Seed was its instrument; Fourth = investigated in the Epilogue after the Arbiter of Ash (PoE1 wiki editors speculate it caused the Great Fire); First = unexplained threat averted in the Epilogue. The full text of the edicts is not given in any source read. Not to be confused with Count Geonor's hanging edicts in Ogham.

chronology.relative: Precursor age, far older than the Vaal and Winter of the World

sources: 'It was depicted in their Edicts, vague murals that depicts the Beast and possibly instructions on how to contain it.'
Return to Kingsmarch: Doryani 'The Third Edict? What is the meaning... of these Edicts?'
Return to Kingsmarch: Hooded One 'It is the Weapon I saw in that third mural'; Enter the Excavated Site: Makoru 'These murals... appear to depict the Weapon... and the Beast'

nodes.name: Trial of Chaos
nodes.summary: A PoE2 Ascension Trial first accessible in Act 3 at the Temple of Chaos via an Inscribed Ultimatum (or the quest item Chimeral Inscribed Ultimatum from Xyclucian). Based on the PoE1 Ultimatum league and overseen by the Trialmaster.
sources: intro: 'The Trialmaster ... oversee the Trials of Chaos'

alt_summaries.summary: Ascension trial in the Temple of Chaos (first in Act 3), a gauntlet run with an Inscribed Ultimatum; the Trialmaster offers modifiers and rewards. Mechanically based on PoE1's Ultimatum.

nodes.name: Trial of the Sekhemas
nodes.summary: A PoE2 Ascension Trial first accessible in Act 2 via the Djinn Barya key (or the quest item Balbala's Barya), a gauntlet of up to 4 floors with bosses including Rattlecage, Hadi and Rafiq, Ashar and Zarokh.

alt_summaries.summary: Ascension trial first accessible in Act 2 via a Djinn Barya on the Relic Altar; a gauntlet governed by Honour, Boons and Afflictions; based on PoE1's Forbidden Sanctum.

nodes.name: Utopia (Twilight Order ideal)
nodes.summary: The Order's promised god-free world ('without gods... without suffering... without the disease of Divinity'), recruited for with 'Accept Utopia! Embrace the saviour!'. Art book: intention is good but its methods are contentious.

nodes.name: Vaal corruption and thaumaturgical technology
nodes.summary: Vaal science combined gem-craft, constructs, mechanical technology and corruption drawn from the Beast; much of it was developed by Doryani and housed at Atzoatl and Utzaal. Its influence resurfaces as Vaal side areas, Vaal skill gems and Vaal Orbs in PoE1.

nodes.name: Vaal sacrifice and Vaal souls
nodes.summary: Vaal bloodpriests discovered that the souls of the recently killed briefly seek another source of life and can be captured in a vaal skill gem to empower it; human and blood sacrifice powered Vaal constructs and society, and slavery supplied victims.

nodes.name: Verisium
nodes.summary: Metal ore found only in fallen meteorites and not native to Wraeclast; Kalguuran runes were typically crafted from it, and in PoE2 Act 4 Dannig forges Verisium Spikes from Verisium Ingots.
sources: ===Runes===: "Runes were typically crafted using Verisium, a type of metal ore found only from fallen meteorites, and not native to Wraeclast."
Bring the Verisium to Dannig / Take the Verisium Spikes from Dannig: Dannig crafts Verisium Spikes from Verisium Ingots
Remnants can contain Verisium used in Runeforging
Seek out the crater of a fallen star, a meteor of pure Verisium

alt_summaries.summary: Ore from remnants and a meteor; enables Runeforging and Runic Ward.

nodes.name: Virtue Gems
nodes.summary: Gems from the Beast, the source of thaumaturgy, buried by Veruso and mined by slaves under Chitus; infused into gemlings. Ubiquitous in Vaal society.

alt_summaries.summary: Azmeri term for virtue gems, which they are forbidden to touch; contact causes a horrific reaction.
Gems discovered under Mount Veruso that the Vaal used to gain great power; Vaal bodies were adorned and later socketed with gems, and the Vaal never shared the secret with the Azmeri.

nodes.name: Humours / Wisps (Wildwood)
nodes.summary: In the Viridian Wildwood the four humours (Primal, Vivid, Wild, Sacred) materialise as wisps. The first three share names with Harvest's Primal, Vivid and Wild Lifeforce colours. Sacred humours are harvested by the ritual altars of the King in the Mists.

nodes.name: Hiveborn
nodes.summary: Breach-spawn into which the Breachlords were evolving; the Keepers of the Flame, founded through Chayula's dreams, exist to destroy them. The Dreamer is revealed to be of the same kind as the Hiveborn.
sources: Lore: the Breachlords began their evolution into the Hiveborn; the Dreamer is the same creature as the Hiveborn

alt_summaries.summary: Mutated Breach monsters spilling into Wraeclast through a stabilised interdimensional link.
Breach monsters invading Wraeclast in the reworked Breach; fought by the Exile and Ailith, source of Graftblood and Hiveblood.

nodes.name: The Lightless (Abyssals)
nodes.summary: Ancient subterranean race created, not born, via necromancy, afraid of light; invaded during the Winter of the World and were driven back underground by the returning sun. Antagonists of Abyss and PoE2 Rise of the Abyssals.
sources: The Winter of the World > The Lightless

alt_summaries.summary: Ancient necromantic race, the Abyssals ('the spawn of the Well of Souls' per the Hooded One), serving Kulemak through Lich Lords; they emerge through Abyss fissures. Ancient alliances fought them for centuries in the Winter of the World.

nodes.name: The Nameless
nodes.summary: Shadowy beings born with the Wildwood as the 'unseen reflection opposite the mortal world'; led by the King in the Mists; Gruthkul was one.

nodes.name: Arakaali, Spinner of Shadows
nodes.summary: Vaal spider-goddess of love and death, worshipped by Azmeri artists; consorts with Silk in the Temple of Decay and is killed as Act 7's boss. A relationship with Sin is hinted.
sources: 'lesser relationships with ... Arakaali' (cites PoE2 Arakaali's Lust)

alt_summaries.summary: Vaal harlot turned fertility goddess and queen, the Spinner of Shadows; held Sin captive; sealed in the Temple of Decay and slain by the Exile in Act 7.
Spinner of Shadows: mortal temptress turned arachnid, Vaal goddess of fertility, first worshipped by the Azmeri; her temple is the Temple of Decay (Act 7).

nodes.name: The Beast
nodes.summary: Divine creature, source of thaumaturgy and corruption, grown by Sin from the Dark Ember beneath Highgate to keep the gods asleep. Has no will of its own; exploited by Doryani, Atziri, Chitus, Malachai. The Exile kills it in Act 4; PoE2 follows a new Beast grown from the stolen Seed of Corruption.

alt_summaries.summary: Gigantic Dark Ember creature sealed under Highgate, killed by the Exile in Act 4; its death weakens the gods' restraint.
Gods-lulling Dark Ember creature killed in Act 4.

Creature grown by Sin from the Dark Ember to lull the gods into sleep and prevent mortal ascension to godhood; killed by the exile in Act 4, which freed the gods and the souls of Malachai's lieutenants.
Ancient divine creature grown from the Seed of Corruption by Sin; in PoE2 a Beast carried across the Vastiri on the Faridun Dreadnought and fed corpses by the Countess's plan.
Ancient divine creature of thaumaturgy, created by Sin from the Seed of Corruption; Atziri and Doryani manipulated it.

nodes.name: Chaos
nodes.summary: Impulse able to see across timelines, once worshipped by Vaal priests; master of the Trialmaster and enemy-of-sorts to Hinekora's fixed prophecies.
sources: intro and section 'Interactions with other characters'
Community Team post: 'Chaos does not know what you truly are...'

alt_summaries.summary: An Impulse, a beyond-godlike being and the flip of the coin, who can see multiple timelines and is the master of the Trialmaster. Worshipped by the Vaal. The Blood Crucible was a pact between Chaos and the Vaal High Priests.

Impulse, a godlike entity that sees all possibilities across timelines and delights in mortals bending chance; once worshipped by the Vaal; master of the Trialmaster; opposed to Order. Aware that the exiles exist in parallel timelines (dev statement).

Impulse of Chaos, not a Vaal god, but a sect of Vaal priests worshipped him; his Temple of Chaos stood on the outskirts of Utzaal. The Trialmaster says Atziri's realm lies beyond his reach and the Vaal fall occurred in every timeline.

nodes.name: Chayula, the Dreamer
nodes.summary: Breachlord known as the Dreamer or Benevolent Dreamer; PoE2 lore shows he aided the Third Pact alliance, was severed from the failed Breachlord merge, and formed the Keepers of the Flame through dreams. After Xesht falls Ailith reveals his ultimate aim is to subjugate all life as obedient thralls.
sources: Lore: the Dreamer is Chayula, a Breachlord
Lore: after Xesht is defeated Ailith tells the player the Dreamer's true intent

alt_summaries.summary: One of five Breachlords (chaos). Boss of Chayula's Domain (male per wiki). As the Dreamer (Keepers league) he opposes the Xesht fusion. Original Breach bosses introduced in 2.5.0 (Chayula to the core game 2.6.0 per wiki version history), removed 3.28.0.
Breachlord worshipped at Atzoatl by the Cult of Purple Flame.

nodes.name: Esh, Forked Thought
nodes.summary: One of five Breachlords. Lightning damage Breachlord. Boss residing in Esh's Domain; Breachstone/Flawless Breachstone via map device (PoE1 2.5.0; domains removed 3.28.0).
sources: boss page: found in Hive Colony, encountered together with the other

alt_summaries.summary: Breachlord (Esh) fought as a paired boss with its counterpart in the Hive Colony (PoE2 0.5); they share a health bar in the final phase and drop the Breachlord Sac.

nodes.name: Garukhan
nodes.summary: Goddess of wind and sky, formerly the Maraketh Sekhema Orbala ('Sekhema of Sekhemas'); freed Sin from the cliff where Innocence's followers had chained him, became his lover and wife and bore Shakari; Sin planted the Dark Ember 'for Garukhan'.
sources: 'Garukhan, Queen of the Wind' (Orbala; Chains of Castigation, Blood of Innocence, Sin 'Garukhan' dialogue)
Relationships: Sin was wed to Garukhan

alt_summaries.summary: Maraketh storm goddess, Queen of the Winds; wife of Sin, mother of Shakari; formerly the hero Orbala, Sekhema of Sekhemas (PoE2). Slain by the Exile in Act 9 at Sin's request.

Maraketh goddess ('Vulture of the Wastes', Queen of the Winds), wife of Sin and mother of Shakari; in PoE2 she is revealed to have been the mortal Sekhema Orbala. Killed in the Quarry in Act 9 after Kira's attempted sacrifice of Oyun. Minor Pantheon god.

The PoE1 wiki's Orbala page says PoE2 identifies Garukhan as the ascended Orbala (mortal Maraketh warrior); the PoE1 wiki and PoE2 quests do not fully confirm this, so it stays inferred. The Horn of the Vastiri quest retraces Orbala's footsteps.

nodes.name: Halani
nodes.summary: Forgotten Maraketh water goddess, found powerless and dying from lack of worship in PoE2 Act 2 Buried Shrines; mother of Azarian.
sources: Walkthrough 'Talk to the Water Goddess' / 'End the Water Goddess' suffering'

alt_summaries.summary: Water goddess lying in a shrine at the heart of Keth. She asks the Exile to burn her with Everburning Cinders to end her suffering.

nodes.name: Hinekora
nodes.summary: Karui goddess, the Mother of Death, ruler of the Halls of the Dead, seer of prophecy; speaks through the Well of Passing and rewards the worthy with the Tattoo of Hinekora.
sources: Peer into the Well of Passing

alt_summaries.summary: Karui Mother of Death; collects souls in the Halls of the Dead, foresees events across timelines, whipped Kitava into the underworld with her hair, and slept after foreseeing the Slumbering of the Gods. Oversees the Trial of the Ancestors.
Karui goddess of death; could not see Doryani in the past.

nodes.name: Kamasa
nodes.summary: Vaal god of Wealth, represented by a monkey; in PoE2 Act 3 monkey-statue temples in Utzaal hold Kamasa treasure.
sources: Orb of Sacrifice named for Kamasa

alt_summaries.summary: Vaal Monkey God of wealth and greed; mentioned in PoE2 Act 2/3 and in PoE1 items.

nodes.name: Kitava
nodes.summary: Karui god of chaos, hunger and corruption (Father of Corruption, the Cannibal King, Black Spirit); invited into Wraeclast by the Eternals per Karui lore, devours Oriath and is slain by the Exile with Sin and Innocence in Act 10.
sources: Lore: 'Karui god of chaos, hunger, and corruption'; final boss of Act 5 and Act 10

alt_summaries.summary: The Karui god of destruction, who awakens after Innocence is defeated. Killed in Act 10 with Sin and a re-awakened Innocence, after Bannon's sacrifice.
Karui god of chaos, hunger and corruption; summoned by Utula at the end of Act 5; the Exile cannot defeat him until Act 10.
Karui god of chaos, hunger and corruption, a cannibal deity who feeds on Oriath; reawakens at the end of Act 5, is the final boss of Acts 5 and 10 and is killed in the Feeding Trough.

nodes.name: Kopec
nodes.summary: Vaal sun god; the Temple of Kopec in Utzaal sealed the time gateway.
sources: Alva: 'Temple of the Sun God, Kopec'

alt_summaries.summary: Vaal god, presumably of sun or fire; PoE2 has the Temple of Kopec.

nodes.name: Kulemak
nodes.summary: Master of the Lightless and creator of the Lich Lords; exalted within the Well of Souls (which arose after The Master Below All 'raged'), he waged the Winter of the World against the surface until the Three Sisters destroyed his mortal form; his soul returned to the Well. Namesake of the Horns of Kulemak (Immortal Syndicate). PoE2 pinnacle of the Well of Souls content.
sources: Hooded One: 'Kulemak, the Lich Lord, master of Undeath'

alt_summaries.summary: Creator and master of the Lightless and Lich Lords; exalted within the Well of Souls (power of necromancy); waged war on the surface, deceived Aul with a bargain for a stone golem, ending the primeval civilisation. Destroyed in mortal form by the Three Sisters; his soul returned to the Well. Appears in PoE2 (Rise of the Abyssal / Abyss).
Abyssal god of undeath whose Well of Souls is in Act 2; lieutenants Amanamu, Ulaman and Kurgal; the Lurking Creature calls Sin 'Stealer of Kulemak's spark'. Relevant to endgame via Tecrod.

Lich Lord, creator and master of the Lightless, exalted in the Well of Souls; the Hooded One calls him 'a dark god... Kulemak, the Lich Lord, master of Undeath' whose body the alliance destroyed countless times though the Well stayed out of reach. Fought as the Vessel of Kulemak via Kulemak's Invitation in the Black Cathedral.

nodes.name: Lunaris
nodes.summary: Eternal/Azmeri moon goddess, sister of Solaris; her rivalry was engineered by Tangmazu. (PoE2 appearance of Solaris/Lunaris by name not verified in the local PoE2 corpus; Maraketh variants Solerai/Lundara and the Three Sisters myth cover PoE2.)

alt_summaries.summary: Minimal node (owned elsewhere): Sun/Moon deity of the Eternal/Templar pantheon.
Azmerian god of the Moon, sister of Solaris and Viridi, worshipped by the Eternal Empire; fought alongside Solaris at the Harbour Bridge in Act 8 after the Moon Orb is taken from Dusk.

nodes.name: The Master Below All
nodes.summary: Ancient being whose rage created the Well of Souls, power source of necromancy; nothing else known.

nodes.name: Ngamahu
nodes.summary: Karui Ancestor/god honoured by a Karui tribe in the Trial of the Ancestors.
sources: Halls of the Dead test; Karui tattoos by god's domain

alt_summaries.summary: Karui goddess of fire, Mother of Fire; honoured in Ngamakanui.

nodes.name: Order
nodes.summary: Impulse opposed to Chaos, representing dominion and control; Hinekora is its servant per wiki analysis; in one timeline Order overcame Chaos through Venarius's enslavement of humanity.

alt_summaries.summary: Impulse opposed to Chaos; almost nothing is known.

nodes.name: Sin
nodes.summary: God, brother (twin, per the stained-glass windows) of Innocence; planted the Dark Ember beneath Highgate from which the Beast grew. In PoE1 he guides the Exile against Kitava; in PoE2 the Hooded One reveals in Act 2 that he is Sin.
sources: 'The Hooded One was likely Sin, owing to his dark appearance, apparent godhood and original planting of the Dark Ember'
intro paragraph 3 (Sin plants the Dark Ember; Beast initiates the Slumber of the Gods)
section 'Lore' (Sin captures Innocence's soul; Sin and the Exile defeat Kitava in Act 10)
Lore: reveals himself as Sin at the end of Act 2
Lore, The Beast, In-game interactions, Path of Exile 2
"I am Sin, the Forgotten One." / Act 6: "I am Sin, Thief of Virtue, and it is mine to take what I will from the defeated"
Quest log 'Speak to the Hooded One in the Shrine to the Northwest'

alt_summaries.summary: A god vilified as Sin, who planted the Dark Ember in Highgate to create the Beast and triggered the Slumber of the Gods. In PoE1 Act 10 the Exile and Sin defeat Kitava.

God, twin brother of Innocence, 'Thief of Virtue', creator of the Beast and Exile's ally in PoE1 Act 5-10 (sources the Pantheon); husband of Garukhan, father of Shakari. In PoE2 he hides as the Hooded One.
Brother of Innocence, creator of the Beast; appears to the Exile in the Chamber of Innocence and saves them from Kitava.

Thief of Virtue, twin brother of Innocence and creator of the Beast via the Dark Ember seed; in Part Two he guides the exile to harvest the souls of risen gods and Malachai's lieutenants to forge a new Dark Ember and defeat Kitava. Returns in PoE2 as 'the Hooded One'.
God Sin, 'Thief of Virtue'. In PoE2 Act 2 the Hooded One reveals himself as Sin and as the creator of the Beast.

PoE1 god, twin brother of Innocence (the stained-glass version of their tale is Templar propaganda), who planted the Dark Ember/Seed beneath Highgate to grow the Beast and lull the gods; in PoE2 he is the Hooded One (revealed in Act 2).
God who created the Beast.

nodes.name: Solaris
nodes.summary: Eternal/Azmeri sun goddess, twin sister of Lunaris; led a rival cult after Tangmazu tricked her into believing Lunaris betrayed her. Sin has her soul captured for the Pantheon in Act 8. (PoE2 appearance of Solaris/Lunaris by name not verified in the local PoE2 corpus; Maraketh variants Solerai/Lundara and the Three Sisters myth cover PoE2.)

alt_summaries.summary: Minimal node (owned elsewhere): Sun/Moon deity of the Eternal/Templar pantheon.

Azmerian god of the Sun, sister of Lunaris and Viridi, recognised and worshipped by the Eternal Empire; she and Lunaris awaken in Act 8 and are summoned to the Harbour Bridge with the Sun and Moon Orbs and killed. Their flavour texts suggest a possible link to the Maraketh Sekhemas Solerai and Lundara (speculative).

nodes.name: Tangmazu
nodes.summary: Trickster god (Tekaru to the Karui, Black Crow to the Ezomytes), Ralakesh's brother, said to have made Solaris and Lunaris fight; listed on the wiki as an NPC related to Delirium and, in PoE2, revealed as the disguised Freya Hartlin whose release triggers a Delirium encounter.
sources: Freya Hartlin reveals herself as Tangmazu
Quest: Journey's End and Tangmazu reveal
Solaris, Lunaris and Viridi footnote on the Raven Trickster

alt_summaries.summary: Trickster god (Raven Trickster / Tekaru / Black Crow), brother of Ralakesh, who caused the Solaris-Lunaris feud. The Strange Voice of Delirium mirrors; in PoE2 he is bound in Kedge Bay by Karui bindings, disguised as Freya Hartlin, and freed in Dark Mists.

Trickster being imprisoned by the Ramako and later Tukohama tribes at Journey's End; disguised as Freya Hartlin, freed with Verisium Spikes, triggering a Delirium encounter. Elder Madox later calls the Raven Trickster 'he of many names and many faces' (identification only implied).

nodes.name: Tasalio
nodes.summary: Karui Ancestor/god honoured by a Karui tribe in the Trial of the Ancestors.

alt_summaries.summary: Karui god of water, Father of Water.

nodes.name: Tawhoa
nodes.summary: Karui Ancestor/god honoured by a Karui tribe in the Trial of the Ancestors.

alt_summaries.summary: Karui god of the forest and birds, Father of the Forest.

nodes.name: The Bodach
nodes.summary: Dark entity fought as the final boss of Legacy of the Maji after the Rite of the Nameless ('Explore the Darkness'; 'Defeat the Bodach'); the official 0.5.0 text says a prison beneath Caer Tarth holds it. At T14+ it is the Ritual pinnacle per a guide.
sources: paragraph 3: Sisters sealed away the Bodach
steps 53-54 'Explore the Darkness', 'Defeat the Bodach'; completion: Defeat The Bodach
The prison beneath it holds the Bodach

alt_summaries.summary: Embodiment of the Unlight sealed away by the Three Sisters in Wildwood Azmeri myth; PoE2 Ritual pinnacle boss in Caer Tarth, tied to the King in the Mists (0.5).

nodes.name: The Draiocht
nodes.summary: Goddess protecting the Azmeri, divided into the Three Sisters Mhacha, Catha, Morrigan who gave themselves to imbue nature; created the Wildwood and forbade gems. Original name lost.

nodes.name: The First Ones
nodes.summary: Animalistic gods worshipped by the Ezomytes, believed to roam the realm of Spirit; their avatars are Spirit Beasts: Saqawal (birds/reptiles, 'Last of the First'), Farrul (hounds/cats/mammals, 'First of the Hunt'), Fenumus (insects, 'First Explorer'), Craiceann (crabs/squid/sea life, 'First of All'). Also The Greatwolf and the Gull.
sources: Craiceann section: avatar of the First Ones

alt_summaries.summary: Group of animalistic Ezomyte gods including Craiceann, Farrul, Fenumus, Saqawal, the Greatwolf and the Gull; roam the realm of Spirit.

nodes.name: Tukohama
nodes.summary: Karui god of war; his tooth slashed Kitava's face. Revived by the Beast's death, he raises the Karui Fortress and is the first god the Exile captures for the Pantheon in Act 6. Kaom claimed to be his son (carvings in Kaom's Stronghold).

alt_summaries.summary: Karui god of war and minor Pantheon god; the first god the exile kills, in his Keep in the Karui Fortress. Defeating him unlocks the first Pantheon power.
Karui god of war; in the Act 4 boss fight Tavakai calls on him ('Lend me your strength') and Tukohama refuses: 'This... is not the Way.'

nodes.name: Tul, Creeping Avalanche
nodes.summary: One of five Breachlords. Cold Breachlord (female per wiki). Boss residing in Tul's Domain; Breachstone/Flawless Breachstone via map device (PoE1 2.5.0; domains removed 3.28.0).
sources: boss page: found in Hive Colony, encountered together with the other

alt_summaries.summary: Breachlord (Tul) fought as a paired boss with its counterpart in the Hive Colony (PoE2 0.5); they share a health bar in the final phase and drop the Breachlord Sac.

nodes.name: Uul-Netol, Unburdened Flesh
nodes.summary: One of five Breachlords. Physical damage Breachlord. Boss residing in Uul-Netol's Domain; Breachstone/Flawless Breachstone via map device (PoE1 2.5.0; domains removed 3.28.0).

nodes.name: Valako
nodes.summary: Karui god of storms and lightning; his jaw became a fish hook, one of Kitava's Torments.
sources: Lani: 'A fish hook that was once the Valako's Jaw'

nodes.name: Viridi
nodes.summary: Third sister of Solaris and Lunaris, Azmeri goddess of the earth, trapped within 'the orb' in Azmeri creation myth; probable namesake of the Viridian Wildwood.

nodes.name: Xesht
nodes.summary: Incomplete union of the Breachlords Xoph, Tul, Esh and Uul-Netol after the five-Breachlord merge failed (Chayula was severed); filled with mindless rage and hunger. PoE1 fought it as Xesht-Ula, the Open Hand; in PoE2 0.5 it is the Breach pinnacle ('Xesht, We That Are One' per a guide), reached through a Breachstone/Realmgate.
sources: Trivia: Xesht is the incomplete fusion of Xoph, Esh, Tul, Uul-Netol; Chayula opposes as the Dreamer
Dialogue "Who is our enemy?": "Xoph... Esh... Tul... Uul-Netol... our melding... failed... They became Xesht."
Lore: failed merge of the five Breachlords; Chayula severed, rest formed Xesht
Lore: failed merge; the rest of the Breachlords formed an incomplete union in the form of Xesht
Xesht: fought by communing with the Dreamer
Xesht, We That Are One: Breach Splinters form a Breachstone, slotted into the Realmgate

alt_summaries.summary: Entity of the Breach (PoE2 wiki: Xesht): the incomplete fusion of four Breachlords (Xoph, Esh, Tul, Uul-Netol) after the planned five-way merger failed; Chayula was severed from the union and opposes it as the Dreamer. Per the Dreamer, Xesht is 'four minds sewn together' filled with endless rage and hunger.

nodes.name: Xoph, Dark Embers
nodes.summary: One of five Breachlords (fire). Boss of Xoph's Domain, accessed via Xoph's Breachstone in a map device (2.5.0; removed from game 3.28.0). Model based on a Marauder; one of four lords fused into Xesht.

nodes.name: Yaomac
nodes.summary: Ancient Vaal god with three serpentine heads, worshipped by Vaalish priests. Ixchel stole his sleeping body for the Order of the Djinn; the Trialmaster refers to Yaomac when the player wins five or more times.

alt_summaries.summary: Vaal shepherd of souls with three serpentine heads who maintains the balance of seasons.
Three-headed serpent Vaal deity, shepherd of Vaal souls and arbiter of the seasons' balance.

nodes.name: Yugul, Reflection of Terror
nodes.summary: Former Vaal scholar of fear who ascended by terrifying children and Vaal leaders; a maw-god killed in the High Gardens.

alt_summaries.summary: Vaal scholar obsessed with fear who used mirrors to petrify terror; ascended through worship; slain by the Exile in Act 8 (Reflection of Terror).
Vaal scholar of fear who ascended to godhood through mirrors that 'petrify fear'; killed by the Exile in PoE1 Act 8.

nodes.name: Ancient Azmeri/Ezomyte Age
aliases: Ancient Azmeri, Ezomyte, Maraketh and Karui Era
nodes.summary: Era of the primeval civilisation, Winter of the World, Lightless war and the ancient Azmeri, Ezomyte, Maraketh and Karui peoples, before the Eternal Empire (1 IC).
sources: sections Primeval civilization, The Azmeri, The Maraketh, The Ezomytes
intro paragraph 2; sections 'The Azmeri', 'The Ezomytes', 'The Karui'

alt_summaries.summary: Post-Winter-of-the-World cultures (Azmeri, Maraketh, Ezomyte, Karui) and the Order of the Djinn that defeated the Lightless.

nodes.name: Eternal Empire (era)
nodes.summary: Umbrella period of the Eternal Empire (Sarn Empire) from Imperialis Conceptus (1 IC) through the Reign of Voll to the Cataclysm (~1339 IC). Split into the era_eternal_empire_rise and era_eternal_empire_fall buckets; the faction itself is faction_eternal_empire.
sources: section '===Imperialis Conceptus (1 IC)===' (start) and '===The Cataclysm (~1339 IC)===' (end)

nodes.name: Eternal Empire Fall
nodes.summary: The later Eternal Empire: Izaro's Lord's Labyrinth (1317 IC), Chitus and the gemling legions, the Purity Rebellion (1333-1334 IC) and the Cataclysm (c. 1339 IC) that ends the empire. Boundary with the 'rise' bucket is a convention.
sources: sections 'Reign of Izaro', 'The Purity Rebellion', 'The Cataclysm (~1339 IC)'

nodes.name: Eternal Empire Rise
nodes.summary: From 1 IC: Tarcus Veruso leads the Azmeri into the lands left by the Vaal and founds Sarn and the Eternal Empire; the empire expands; the Night of a Thousand Ribbons (c. 334 IC) ends Romira's reign.
sources: section 'The Eternal Empire': 'Imperialis Conceptus (1 IC)', 'Reign of Tarcus Veruso', 'Night of a Thousand Ribbons'

nodes.name: Interlude Between Games
nodes.summary: About 20 years between the defeat of Kitava and the PoE2 prelude: Count Geonor, Ogham, and the release of the Seed of Corruption.
sources: section 'Prelude / Count Geonor' ('twenty years after the defeat of Kitava')

nodes.name: PoE2 (era umbrella)
nodes.summary: Umbrella for the PoE2-era buckets: the Acts 1-6 campaign and interludes (era_poe2_campaign) and endgame and league storylines (era_poe2_endgame). Begins after the ~20-year interlude following the PoE1 kill of the Beast. Meta grouping only.

chronology.relative: c. 20 years after the Beast's death

sources: paragraph 3: 'An exile was responsible for killing the Beast around 20 years prior to the events of Path of Exile 2'

nodes.name: PoE2 Campaign
nodes.summary: The PoE2 campaign: the Exile chases the Seed of Corruption across Wraeclast, starting in Ogham (Act 1).

nodes.name: PoE2 Endgame
nodes.summary: PoE2 endgame storylines after the campaign. Not covered in detail in this domain.
sources: section 'Notes' (endgame sections not covered by this domain)

nodes.name: Post-Cataclysm Oriath
nodes.summary: Oriath, the island unaffected by the Cataclysm, becomes a Templar theocracy; the Templar Courts and Chamber of Innocence are built under High Templar Avarius. Roughly 260 years pass before PoE1.

nodes.name: Post-Vaal Dark Age
nodes.summary: Ruins of the Vaal, the surviving Vaal absorbed into the Azmeri, and the Kalguur expedition that colonised and failed on Wraeclast.

chronology.relative: between the Vaal Cataclysm and 1 IC

nodes.name: Precursor Era
nodes.summary: Age of the Precursor civilisation, the only culture wholly predating the Winter of the World; its apex lies further before the Vaal than the Vaal lie before the present.

chronology.relative: before the Winter of the World

alt_summaries.summary: The Precursor civilization, the only culture that wholly predates the Winter of the World, with technology far beyond later peoples.

nodes.name: Primordial Wraeclast
nodes.summary: Earliest prehistory: a molten world with Kalandra trapped in her lake, the Titans, the Winter of the World and the Lightless attack. The wiki says the order of prehistoric events is unclear.

chronology.relative: before the Vaal; earliest prehistory (exact years unknown)

sources: Prehistory: 'When Wraeclast was a primordial molten world of ooze and magma'

alt_summaries.summary: Earliest age of Wraeclast: a molten world of ooze and magma inhabited by Titans, in which Kalandra found her lake. Chronology is explicitly unclear.

nodes.name: Vaal Era
nodes.summary: The Vaal Empire under Queen Atziri, the use of virtue gems and sacrifice, ending in the Vaal Cataclysm.

alt_summaries.summary: Period of the Vaal civilisation up to the Vaal Cataclysm (c. 400 BIC).

nodes.name: Atziri trapped in the crimson nightmare
nodes.summary: After the Cataclysm Atziri kept her beauty at the cost of her humanity, relegated to a nightmare realm where sacrificed Vaal rise and die repeatedly; her influence later seeps back via Vaal side areas and corruption.

nodes.name: Aul's Final Ritual
nodes.summary: In his last moments Aul rapidly crystallises his citadel with azurite, becoming the Crystal King.
sources: Primeval civilization > Aul: 'In the final moments of his reign, he enacted the final ritual, encasing his palace in crystals'

nodes.name: Aul and Kulemak's Bargain
nodes.summary: Weakened Kulemak offers Aul 'untold power and mastery' for a single golem; the golem is infused with necromancy and the first Lightless/possessed golems result, ultimately toppling the primeval civilisation.

nodes.name: Release Balbala in Traitor's Passage
nodes.summary: Using Risu's passage, the Exile climbs Traitor's Passage and defeats Balbala, releasing the sealed Djinn.

nodes.name: Keth: the Essence of Water
nodes.summary: Following the sand-buried city of Keth, the Exile defeats Azarian, the Forsaken Son, and burns the Water Goddess Halani at her request to recover the Essence of Water.
sources: Walkthrough 'Defeat Azarian' / 'End the Water Goddess' suffering'

nodes.name: Sin creates the Beast
nodes.summary: Sin planted the Dark Ember/Seed of Corruption beneath Highgate and nurtured it into the Beast to suppress the gods and end mortal ascension. PoE2 wiki adds that Sin sought Kalandra's cryptic advice and found the Seed in a Precursor ruin.
sources: paragraph 2: Sin ... sought the ancient being Kalandra ... found a Precursor ruin containing the Seed of Corruption

alt_summaries.summary: Sin plants Dark Ember.

nodes.name: Flame Ruby from the Titan Grotto
nodes.summary: Through the Titan Grotto's Rite of Flame, the Exile defeats Zalmarath, the Colossus, and recovers the Flame Ruby for Zarka.

nodes.name: Capture Doryani in the Black Chambers
nodes.summary: The Exile fights through Aggorat to the Black Chambers, rescues Alva, and captures Doryani, who agrees to help contain the Beast with a piece of the Precursor weapon.
sources: Quest 'Capture Doryani for his knowledge of the Beast'

alt_summaries.summary: The Exile defeats Doryani in the Black Chambers; Alva convinces him to follow them to the future and help contain the Beast.

nodes.name: Doryani joins the Exile and the Hooded One in the present
nodes.summary: In the present Doryani confirms he holds one piece of an ancient anti-Corruption weapon; Alva proposes Kingsmarch as a base, and the Hooded One decides the group should travel south to Ngamakanui to find the other pieces.

nodes.name: Board the Dreadnought and defeat Jamanra, the Abomination
nodes.summary: The Exile boards the Dreadnought; Jamanra the Abomination fights, the Countess escapes, and Asala beheads Jamanra. The Beast escapes with the Countess once more.
sources: Quest 'Defeat Jamanra, the Abomination' / 'Speak to Asala'

nodes.name: Earn passage on the Ardura caravan
nodes.summary: The Exile defeats the Sun Clan hyenas and their leader Rathbreaker for Zarka, who admits the Exile to the Ardura akhara as a jingakh.

nodes.name: The Cataclysm
nodes.summary: c. 1339 IC; Malachai takes control of the Beast; Empire falls.
sources: section 'The Cataclysm (~1339 IC)' and 'Reign of Voll'

alt_summaries.summary: Malachai uses the Rapture Device to breach the Belly of the Beast, triggering the Cataclysm around 1339 IC. It ends the Eternal Empire and Voll's reign, and its effects are mostly confined to the Wraeclast landmass.
Eternal Empire's destruction.

nodes.name: Fall of the Primeval Civilization
nodes.summary: The primeval civilisation is toppled by possessed golems (probably the Lightless), as the Winter of the World approaches.

nodes.name: First Kalguuran expedition to Wraeclast
nodes.summary: Expedition commissioned by Cadigan III after the Vaal Cataclysm 'Omen'; led by Olroth (Knights of the Sun), Uhtred (Order of the Chalice), Vorana (Black Scythe) and Medved (Druids of the Broken Circle); poisoned journey; colonisation; trade with Karui and Azmeri; gem panic; eventual collapse.

chronology.relative: Thousands of years before PoE1; soon after the Vaal Cataclysm

alt_summaries.summary: Centuries-old expedition ordered by Cadigan III including Knights of the Sun, Black Scythe, Druids of the Broken Circle, Priests of the Chalice and Remembrancers; it taught the Ezomytes runesmithing and ended in tragedy.

nodes.name: Founding of the Order of the Djinn
nodes.summary: Ahkeli and a dekhara of surviving Maraketh found the Order, using golems and relics of power to push back the Lightless and save the Vastiri Plains.

nodes.name: Founding of Oriath
nodes.summary: Templars banished from the Azmeri found Oriath.

nodes.name: Great Fire
nodes.summary: Ezomyte cataclysm: the First Ones, unhonoured, spill fire out of a mountain; leaders turned to ash, survivors fed on tainted grain from Mother Gull. PoE2 reveals it is the Winter of the World.

nodes.name: Great Wasting
nodes.summary: Karui name for the apocalyptic age of horror and famine also called the Great Fire (Ezomyte) and Winter of the World (Maraketh); Karui ancestors and Maraketh gods are said to emerge in it.

nodes.name: First battle at the Halani Gates
nodes.summary: The Exile opens the gates with Asala; Jamanra, the Risen King, is fought at the gates and retreats behind an impassable sandstorm (Faridun page), while the Countess escapes.
sources: Quest 'Open the third Gate' / 'Return to the Ardura Caravan'

nodes.name: The Hooded One reveals he is Sin
nodes.summary: At a shrine northwest of the caravan, the Hooded One confesses he is Sin, the Thief of Virtue, and that he created the Beast; he sends the Exile south into the long-ago Vaal jungles to find a way to drain the Beast.
sources: Quest log 'Speak to the Hooded One in the Shrine to the Northwest' (quote 'I am... a god. I am the Thief of Virtue. I am Sin.')
[77:11] 'I am the thief of virtue.' / [77:14] 'I am sin.' (Gavryn, Act 2 full dialogue, auto-captions)

nodes.name: Recreate the Horn of the Vastiri
nodes.summary: With Zarka, the Exile reforges the Horn of the Vastiri from the three sub-quest items to counter Jamanra's sandstorm, retracing Orbala's footsteps.
sources: Quest log 'Recreate the Horn of the Vastiri'

nodes.name: Imperialis Conceptus
nodes.summary: Founding of the Eternal Empire (1 IC).

alt_summaries.summary: Tarcus Veruso leads the Azmeri down into the lands left by the Vaal and founds Sarn at 1 IC, marking the start of the Eternal calendar and the Eternal Empire.

nodes.name: Kalandra Trapped in the Lake
nodes.summary: Kalandra enters the primordial lake out of curiosity and can never leave: every escape returns her to the lake with no memory.
sources: Lore: Ancient Etchings; History of Wraeclast 'The Lake of Kalandra'

alt_summaries.summary: Kalandra entered the Lake out of curiosity in the primordial era and found herself unable to leave, forgetting each attempt.

nodes.name: Kalguuran Expedition to Wraeclast
nodes.summary: After the Vaal Cataclysm's omens, King Cadigan III sends an expedition with the Triskelion Flame led by Olroth, Uhtred, Vorana and Medved; they colonise Vaal ruins, until horrors, a priesthood plot and the loss of the Flame destroy the colony.

alt_summaries.summary: After the Vaal Cataclysm, a Kalguur expedition (led by Olroth, Uhtred, Vorana and Medved) arrives, colonises, and collapses. The Triskelion Flame is lost and famine follows; the wiki says who sabotaged the port is unknown.

nodes.name: Lightless Invasion
nodes.summary: After ash blocked the sun, the Lightless surface and devastate the primeval civilisation, felled Titans and the Maraketh/Azmeri cultures; a coalition under the Third Pact opposes them.
sources: intro; The Winter of the World

nodes.name: Lord's Labyrinth Opened
nodes.summary: Izaro opens the Lord's Labyrinth on the second Galvano of Azmeri, 1317 IC. Chitus wins it by betraying Weylin, and then seals Izaro inside.
sources: section 'The Lord's Labyrinth' and 'Reign of Chitus'

nodes.name: Slay Count Geonor in Ogham Manor
nodes.summary: The Exile infiltrates Ogham Manor and kills Count Geonor, freeing Ogham; Oriana escapes with the Beast, and the Hooded One sends the Exile east toward the Vastiri.
sources: Quest 'Kill the Mad Wolf' / 'Return to Town'

nodes.name: Maraketh Golden Age
nodes.summary: Roughly a thousand years of glory after Solerai and Lundara expelled the Lightless, in a lush Vastiri of seven rivers; ended when the Beast silenced the gods.

nodes.name: Drain the lake through the Matlan Waterways
nodes.summary: The Exile powers the Infested Barrens altar with the large Soul Core and activates the Matlan Waterways, revealing the Sunken City of Utzaal.
sources: Quest 'Activate The Matlan Waterways' / 'Talk to Alva'

nodes.name: Rudja and the Faridun defector at Mawdun Mine
nodes.summary: At Mawdun Quarry and Mine, the Exile defeats Rudja and frees the defector Risu, who reveals Jamanra's plan to feed the Beast and that the Halani Gates are closed.
sources: Quest 'Defeat Rudja, Dread Engineer' / 'Talk to Risu about the closed Gates'

nodes.name: Night of a Thousand Ribbons
nodes.summary: Burning of Sarn in protest against Romira; later festival where Chitus was assassinated.

alt_summaries.summary: Around 334 IC, Sarn burns in protest at Emperor Romira's cannibal banquet and incest, and Romira is deposed. The date is still celebrated after reconstruction.

nodes.name: Oriath destroyed by Sirus
nodes.summary: PoE1 Conquerors of the Atlas: Oriath is completely destroyed by Sirus, leaving it devastated; PoE2 states the world believed Oriath abandoned twenty years ago after crises.

alt_summaries.summary: Sirus used his own map device to enter Oriath and burn it down; Kirac took a blow meant for Zana; the Exile defeated him. In Siege timeline an unknown exile dealt Sirus a near-fatal blow at the cost of her life.

nodes.name: The Trials of Chaos (PoE2 Act 3 quest)
nodes.summary: Optional Act 3 quest: after obtaining an Inscribed Ultimatum (or the Chimeral Inscribed Ultimatum from Xyclucian), the Exile places it in the Temple of Chaos offering and completes the Trialmaster's Challenges for 2 Ascendancy Points. The PoE2 entry point to the Trial of Chaos ascension trial.
sources: Infobox (act 3, optional, start 'Acquire an Inscribed Ultimatum', boss Xyclucian, the Chimera); '===Place the Inscribed Ultimatum in the Temple Offering===' and '===Quest Complete=== (2 Ascendancy Points)'
Access section (Chimeral Inscribed Ultimatum from Xyclucian; Temple of Chaos offering); lead ('based on Ultimatum from PoE1')

nodes.name: Exile travels to Utzaal's past
nodes.summary: The Exile and Alva use the gateway to reach Utzaal before the Cataclysm to learn of the Beast.

nodes.name: Arrival in Kingsmarch
nodes.summary: Exile, Hooded One and Doryani reach Kingsmarch to find the Weapon; Doryani laments science never recovered; the Hooded One says the Kalguurans 'have potential'.

nodes.name: Alliance plan against Oriath
nodes.summary: The Hooded One decides to call the Ezomytes, Maraketh and Vaal (Doryani's reserves) to war before assaulting Oriath; the Karui are already allied.

nodes.name: Exile defeats Benedictus
nodes.summary: In the Excavation the Countess leaves Benedictus to hold the Exile; he is defeated, and Kanu, begging to be taken along, reveals the Beast is in Oriath before Tavakai strikes him down.
sources: Confront Kanu and the First Herald; Defeat Benedictus

alt_summaries.summary: Act 4: after the Countess flees to Oriath, the Exile defeats Benedictus in the Excavation; Kanu then names Oriath and is killed by Tavakai.

nodes.name: Tavakai defeated at Heart of the Tribe
nodes.summary: Tavakai fights in three phases; Tukohama rejects him ('This... is not the Way'); the Exile defeats him.

nodes.name: Exile defeats Torvian
nodes.summary: On Arastas the Exile defeats Torvian, Hand of the Saviour, after the Twilight Order ambush at the church.
sources: Defeat Torvian, Hand of the Saviour

alt_summaries.summary: Act 4: the Exile defeats Torvian, Hand of the Saviour on Arastas.

nodes.name: Freeing the Trickster at Journey's End
nodes.summary: Exile frees 'Freya Hartlin' with Verisium Spikes; she reveals herself as Tangmazu, triggering a Delirium encounter with Omniphobia.

nodes.name: Charter of the Aurora May
nodes.summary: Alva introduces Rog, who sells a Boat Charter for Vaal treasure; Makoru and Kanu will take the Exile to the most dangerous islands.
sources: Talk to Alva; Take the Boat Charter

nodes.name: Island search for weapon pieces
nodes.summary: The Exile sails the Karui islands (e.g. Isle of Kin, Shrike Island, Whakapanu, Abandoned Prison) to find the three Weapon pieces, whose island locations rotate; bosses include Krutog, Diamora, the Prisoner and the Scourge of the Skies. Kedge Bay is separate Dark Mists content.

nodes.name: Hooded One recalls Precursor script
nodes.summary: On the first and second Weapon pieces the Hooded One recognises Precursor writing from a faded mortal memory (a woman's lap, a vivid book; later: sent to live among the Azmeri with a brother and sister, but earlier 'somewhere else' with works of stone, metal and glass).
sources: Witness the Hooded One (1st and 2nd pieces)
Witness The Hooded One (first and second pieces)

alt_summaries.summary: Weapon pieces carry Precursor writing the Hooded One partly recognises from a mortal childhood: a book in a woman's lap, life 'somewhere else' with stone, metal and glass before being sent to the Azmeri with his brother and sister.

nodes.name: Weapon reforged; Third Edict revealed
aliases: The Weapon is reforged; Third Edict revealed
nodes.summary: In the Excavated Site the Hooded One reforges the Weapon and Tavakai seizes it; back in Kingsmarch the Hooded One reads the inscription 'The instrument of the Third Edict', made to cleanse Corruption and destroy the Beast.
sources: Witness the Hooded One reforge the Weapon; Return to Kingsmarch

alt_summaries.summary: The Hooded One reforges the Weapon in the Excavated Site; Tavakai seizes it. Back in Kingsmarch the Hooded One reads the inscription: 'The instrument of the Third Edict.'

nodes.name: Sin cures Tavakai and Makoru
nodes.summary: The Hooded One, called Sin in the quest log, cures Tavakai and Makoru of Blood Fever with the Weapon; Tavakai pledges the Karui to fight Oriana.
sources: Witness Sin cure Tavakai and Makoru

nodes.name: Tavakai seizes the Weapon
nodes.summary: After the reforging Tavakai takes the Weapon for the Karui and flees to Ngakanu with Makoru; the Hooded One warns of its Corruption.
sources: Witness the Hooded One reforge the Weapon

nodes.name: Utopia on Arastas
nodes.summary: Missionary Lorandis sends the Exile to Arastas to swear an oath to the Saviour; Servitor Marius offers Utopia; refusal completes the quest, and Benedictus and Kanu's treachery follow.

nodes.name: Infiltrating Oriath (PoE2 Act 5, datamined)
nodes.summary: Datamined Act 5 Normal quest listed by PoE2DB after The Siege of Oriath; the table gives no description. Unconfirmed until Act 5 is released.
sources: Act 5 Quest table: 'Infiltrating Oriath' row (Normal; reward none listed)
Act 5 section: '(planned for full release)' (wiki lists no Act 5 quests)

nodes.name: No Rest for the Blighted (PoE2 Act 5, datamined)
nodes.summary: Datamined Act 5 Normal quest listed by PoE2DB; its reward is labelled [DNT-UNUSED] Blighted Core Bomb, so it may not be in the live game.
sources: Act 5 Quest table: 'No Rest for the Blighted' row (Normal; reward [DNT-UNUSED] Blighted Core Bomb)
Act 5 section: '(planned for full release)' (wiki lists no Act 5 quests)

nodes.name: Assault on Oriath (planned Act 5)
nodes.summary: Announced Act 5: arrive in Oriath hunting the Beast; datamined quests The Siege of Oriath, Infiltrating Oriath, etc.

nodes.name: Pinned Down (PoE2 Act 5, datamined)
nodes.summary: Datamined Act 5 Normal quest listed by PoE2DB; reward Reefsteel Greaves. No description in the datamine.
sources: Act 5 Quest table: 'Pinned Down' row (Normal; reward Reefsteel Greaves)
Act 5 section: '(planned for full release)' (wiki lists no Act 5 quests)

nodes.name: Pleasure and Pain (PoE2 Act 5, datamined)
nodes.summary: Datamined Act 5 Normal quest listed by PoE2DB; reward Rogue's Marker x5. No description in the datamine.
sources: Act 5 Quest table: 'Pleasure and Pain' row (Normal; reward Rogue's Marker x5)
Act 5 section: '(planned for full release)' (wiki lists no Act 5 quests)

nodes.name: Plumbing the Depths (PoE2 Act 5, datamined)
